transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-23 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 mins
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samir (CSM) -- Jordan (PM, Acme), Priya (Staff Eng), Diego (Data Eng), Kelvin (Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: integration status, SDK function-calls, structured output formatting, and blockers.
[00:12] Jordan: Yep, we got the invite, thx. we've run the basic text generation flows, now we're trying to wire up the function/tool calling so the app can synthesize structured order objects and call downstream inventory microservices.
[00:25] Priya: the main ask from eng is determinism of structured output, like we need JSON outputs with specific keys and types, and when there's a parse error it should fail loudly.
[00:39] Maya: totally, that's what function-calling + structured-output is for. for the SDK we showed last week, there are two patterns: implicit tool calling via "tools" array, and explicit function call where the model returns a call with the function name and args. you can validate against a JSON schema on the client.
[01:05] Priya: quick q, does Redwood's runtime guarantee the model will always produce valid JSON? sometimes GPT-family models hallucinate keys.
[01:15] Alex: good question. we don't guarantee 100% but the SDK has built-in response schema validation and will surface parsing errors. plus we recommend a small post-parse validator step. also caching/prefixing helps for stable outputs.
[01:36] Diego: i noticed under high load we saw more truncated responses. is that coming from the token limit or from the runtime?
[01:45] Maya: likely token cutoffs; on our hosted endpoints we stream tokens but if application-level timeouts are short you'll see truncation perceived as partial responses. we can tune max_tokens and prefix caching to reduce cost.
[02:05] Kelvin: security question - where are the function arguments logged? we need to ensure any PII in args isn't retained in logs per our policy.
[02:14] Samir: good call. Redwood can mask or skip logging for configured routes. we'll share the log redaction config and KMS integration notes.
[02:28] Jordan: on the SDK snippet you sent earlier, the function schema uses snake_case, we prefer camelCase; any pitfalls?
[02:36] Maya: it's just convention; the model doesn't care but JSON schema enforcement can map keys. we'll include sample snippet showing camelCase outputs and a small mapper.
[02:50] Alex: i'd like to walk through the small demo Priya ran last night. Priya, can you summarize results?
[02:56] Priya: sure. so we wired the SDK -> function call flow. most calls returned a well-formed JSON object with fields orderId, items[], totalCents. about 8% of calls had minor format issues - missing price field or an array item as string instead of object. those were clustered on longer prompts where user message included free-text notes.
[03:22] Diego: we also recorded tail latencies - p50 180ms, p95 680ms in our region. under parallelism we saw some variance, p99 spiking to ~1.2s.
[03:37] Maya: those numbers are consistent. we can reduce p95 by enabling small batching windows and using the dedicated inference profiles or higher-priority routing. tradeoff is cost.
[03:50] Jordan: what's the effort to try a short dedicated window for the pilot?
[03:54] Alex: we can spin up a short Dedicated trial for a week, or alternatively use reserved capacity burst policies. i'll put options in the follow-up email.
[04:05] Priya: on error handling - what pattern do you recommend for retries when function-calls return parse errors?
[04:12] Maya: best is deterministic retry with slight prompt modification: e.g., add "Return strictly valid JSON following this schema" then validate and if still fails, fallback to a secondary simpler model variant or synchronous validation microservice. we can supply a retry wrapper in the SDK.
[04:34] Alex: i'll send that wrapper.
[04:36] [05:10] (crosstalk) Jordan: also need to know about regional routing - can we keep calls in us-east-1 only for data residency?
[05:20] Samir: yes you can pin region in the request config or route policy. we'll include that in docs.
[05:29] Priya: one more thing: structured outputs sometimes include numeric strings like ""1000"" instead of 1000 and that breaks our downstream services. any transforms from Redwood?
[05:40] Maya: the SDK has coercion helpers - we can coerce types post-parse, but we prefer the model produce correct types. we'll include examples and a small schema validator snippet.
[05:52] Alex: let's go into a short code walkthrough; Maya do you want to share screen? (note: recording omitted)
[06:02] Maya: sure, but i'll narrate the snippet. sample: 
 - client.call({ model: 'rwi-std-1', input: prompt, functions: [{name:'createOrder', schema: {...}}], validateSchema: true, onInvalid: 'raise' })
[06:27] Priya: that looks close to our implementation. what's the recommended timeout for order creation flows?
[06:33] Maya: 2s end-to-end is common for interactive UI; batch/async flows can be 5-10s. also for inventory microservice calls you may want to queue and ack immediately.
[06:45] Diego: can the SDK stream partial structured output? e.g., stream large arrays of items?
[06:52] Maya: streaming structured output is experimental; we can stream tokens but assembling a valid JSON incrementally is tricky. suggestion: stream item chunks as separate tool calls or paginate responses.
[07:05] Jordan: will that affect cost significantly?
[07:08] Maya: it may increase token overhead but reduces latency for UI; cost delta depends on prompt design.
[07:16] Alex: security follow-up - Kelvin, any blocking concerns?
[07:20] Kelvin: we need proof that keys are customer-managed or isolated; also audit logs for function args with redaction.
[07:28] Samir: understood, i'll attach KMS options: customer-managed CMKs via our integration and audit log filters.
[07:35] Priya: one last performance test: can Redwood simulate 500 RPS with our sample prompts?
[07:41] Maya: yep, we'll run a benchmark. schedule a 1h window and we'll do a warm-up and then ramp to target.
[07:49] Alex: great. wrapping up - recap and next steps.
[07:53] Jordan: sounds good.
[08:00] Alex: Action items: share code snippets, run integration, run benchmark, send security docs. we'll follow up in email with attachments: example SDK snippet, sample function schema JSON, and a short eval spreadsheet template.
[08:18] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions present (e.g., "kay-vee cache" for KV cache, names sometimes shortened). References: sample snippet link: https://redwood.example.com/poc/snippets/createOrder (private link), security doc link: https://redwood.example.com/poc/security-acme (private).
